name: App shell
description: The frame of a web app: a fixed-width sidebar (brand, navigation, footer) beside a main area, filling the viewport. The two scroll independently. On phones the sidebar either stacks above the content as a single row that scrolls sideways, or — with a top bar — becomes a drawer that a menu button opens.

classes.ayy-app-shell: Root. A viewport-high (100dvh) grid: sidebar column (15rem) and a main column. Neither column grows the page; each scrolls on its own. Sets position: relative (the drawer and its scrim are placed inside it). To embed the shell in a box with a fixed height, set block-size: 100% on it.
classes.ayy-app-shell__sidebar: The <aside>: surface background, hairline on its inline-end edge, brand at the top, nav below, footer pinned to the bottom. Scrolls vertically when its content is taller than the viewport.
classes.ayy-app-shell__brand: Logo / product name link at the top of the sidebar.
classes.ayy-app-shell__nav: <nav> holding the links, stacked vertically (side by side on phones).
classes.ayy-app-shell__link: Destination link. aria-current="page" marks the page you're on: it gets a tint and a heavier weight.
classes.ayy-app-shell__group: A headed section of the nav: a __group-label over a __list. Groups after the first get a hairline above them.
classes.ayy-app-shell__group-label:
The group's heading: a small uppercase

. Give it an id and point the list's aria-labelledby at it.
classes.ayy-app-shell__list: The <ul> of a group. Each <li> holds a link, a link followed by a __sublist, or a __collapse.
classes.ayy-app-shell__sublist: A nested <ul> of child links, indented along a guide line. One level only. Follows a parent link, or sits inside a __collapse. Give it an aria-label when it follows a link.
classes.ayy-app-shell__collapse: A native <details> for a group of child links that opens and closes. Its <summary class="ayy-app-shell__link"> is the toggle, with a chevron at the inline end; put the links in a __sublist inside it. Add `open` when it holds the current page.
classes.ayy-app-shell__link--sub: Modifier for a child link inside a __sublist: a smaller control and a lighter weight.
classes.ayy-app-shell__footer: Pinned to the bottom of the sidebar (the end of the row on phones): settings, account, help link. Keep it short.
classes.ayy-app-shell__main: The <main> content column. Scrolls on its own and has the page gutter.
classes.ayy-app-shell__bar: Phone top bar, first child of the shell: holds the __toggle, the brand and maybe a search button. Hidden from 48rem. Its presence switches the phone layout from the sideways row to a drawer: the sidebar keeps its full layout (groups, sub-lists, collapses) and slides in from the inline-start edge over a scrim.
classes.ayy-app-shell__toggle: The menu button in the __bar (combine with ayy-button ayy-button--ghost ayy-button--icon). Its aria-expanded is the drawer's state: "true" shows the drawer. connectAppShell() / <ayy-app-shell> / React AppShell manage it.

js: appShellClass, appShellSidebarClass, appShellBrandClass, appShellNavClass, appShellLinkClass, appShellFooterClass, appShellMainClass, appShellGroupClass, appShellGroupLabelClass, appShellListClass, appShellSublistClass, appShellCollapseClass, appShellLinkSubClass, appShellBarClass, appShellToggleClass constants; connectAppShell(shell) wires the phone drawer and returns a cleanup; appShellMenuIcon (the Hugeicons menu icon as SVG markup).

props.label: The toggle row: an icon and a short label.

a11y: The sidebar is an <aside> (a complementary landmark) and the content is a <main>: one <main> per page, and no other element with that landmark.
Keep one <nav aria-label="Main"> in the sidebar. Give a second nav (say, a settings menu) its own label.
Mark the current page with aria-current="page". The link also gets a tint and a heavier weight, so colour is not the only cue; High Contrast mode fills it with the system highlight.
Put a .ayy-skip-link before the shell, pointing at an id on <main>, so keyboard users can jump past the sidebar.

Group with a heading and a list: the

label names the

    through aria-labelledby, so a screen reader announces "Foundations, list, 5 items".
A collapse is a native <details>: Enter and Space toggle it, and the open state is exposed for you. Don't add aria-expanded to the <summary>.
Mark the current child with aria-current="page" and open its collapse. A closed collapse that holds the current page is drawn bolder, so the location isn't hidden.
Both columns are scroll containers. If a column can scroll but holds nothing focusable, give it tabindex="0" so keyboard users can scroll it.

The drawer's toggle is a real <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the sidebar (set for you). Opening moves focus to the first link in the drawer and makes the rest of the shell inert; Esc closes it and returns focus to the toggle.
The closed drawer is visibility: hidden, so its links are out of the tab order and the accessibility tree until it opens.
do: Use the app shell as the outer layout of a signed-in app or dashboard: a persistent list of destinations next to the page content.
Reach for it once there are five or more top-level destinations that should stay one click away.
Group destinations under a heading once there are more than about six; one group can hold up to a dozen links.
Use a collapse when a parent has children that are destinations in their own right and you'd otherwise scroll past them; keep the tree one level deep.
Use a link followed by a __sublist when the parent is itself a page and its children are sections of it (Colors → Surfaces, Text…).
Keep to one line per link: an icon and a short label.
Put account and help links in the footer, not among the destinations.
Keep the footer to one or two compact items (settings, a user menu): on phones it joins the scrolling row.
Add a __bar once phones need the nested nav (groups, sub-lists, collapses) or there are more than about five top-level links: the drawer keeps the whole tree.
For a phone app with three to five destinations, use a Bottom nav instead of the drawer, or alongside it for the most frequent ones.
dont: Don't use it for a marketing site or a content page — use Navbar and Sections.
Don't use it to switch views of one object inside a page — use Tabs.
Don't nest deeper than one level, and don't put a collapse inside a collapse.
Don't rely on the phone row for nested items: it shows top-level links only. Headings, sub-lists and collapses are left out; add a __bar to get a drawer that keeps them.
Don't make a collapse the only way to reach a page the user needs often.
Don't nest a second app shell, and don't put a Navbar above it: the sidebar is the site navigation.
Don't scroll the page body as well; the shell already fills the viewport.
Don't give the sidebar its own background colour; the surface token follows every theme.
Don't keep the drawer open as a persistent panel on phones, and don't open it on page load.

element.children: A <div class="ayy-app-shell"> with a __bar holding a __toggle. The toggle opens and closes the sidebar drawer on phones; Esc, the scrim, a link in the drawer or widening past 48rem close it. Without a bar it does nothing.
